headline: Winners and losers: Wade glows, Cullen's darts go cold
standfirst: Three players who left Wolverhampton on the up, three who need a reset before the Players Championship Finals, each with the number that tells the story.
body: A big weekend leaves a trail, so here is who walked away smiling and who is staring at the ceiling. The numbers are our own: recent form against each player's 12-month average.

UP: Gerwyn Price. The Iceman waited five years for a major and finally had one in his hands again in the Grand Slam final. He is a top-three player once more, and he arrives in Minehead as the man to dodge.

UP: James Wade. The Machine averaged 100.27 at the Grand Slam, and across his last three events he is at 98.82 against a 12-month figure of 95.11. At world number seven, that is a player running hot at the right moment.

UP: Martin Schindler. The German sits 20th and has averaged 96.41 across his last three events, comfortably above his 93.02 for the year. Quiet, steady, dangerous. Nobody will want him in their section.

DOWN: Joe Cullen. The Rockstar is the coldest player on the tour right now. His last three events average 84.16 against a 12-month figure of 93.19, a drop of more than nine points, and the World Grand Prix reading of 78.91 was the worst of the lot. Ranked 33rd, he needs a quick fix.

DOWN: Gary Anderson. The Flying Scotsman is 16th in the world and has slipped to 92.57 recently against 98.22 over the year. That is a gap of 5.65 points, and for a player of his class it is a flashing light, not a blip.
DOWN: Martin Lukeman. Smash slid from 43 to 68 in the world rankings, a fall of 25 places and the heaviest on the board. Players around him are catching up fast.
Our view: Cullen is the one to worry about. Anderson can find his scoring in a single good night. A slump this deep is harder to shake off in a short-format weekend like Minehead.
